Ensure that staff are educated that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There were cans of cheese sauce that were observed to be in a hot holding cabinet. The employee stated that they put them in there to make it easier for the cheese sauce to come out. The hot holding cabinet has an ambient temperature of 136F, which is essentially cooking the cheese sauce in the can. Cans are not meant to be used as a cooking vessel, as they have a plastic liner in them that can expose the cheese sauce to adulteration when heated up. CORRECTED- The cans were removed from the hot holding cabinet and it was discussed to put the cheese sauce in containers to cook them in the future. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a box of raw ribeyes on the top shelf of a cooler, above a container of ready-to-eat sauce. CORRECTED- The box of ribeyes was moved to the bottom of the cooler. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following TCS food items were observed to be stored past the 7-day date-marking:

1. Orange juice with a use-by date of 10/12/2026. 
2. A container of creamy horseradish portioned cups (made in-house) with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
3. A container of Cajun ranch (made in-house) with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
4. A container of cooked grits with a make date of 10/19/2026. 
5. A container of Au Jus with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
6. A container of maid-rite meat with a make date of 10/18/2026. 
7. A container of bean salad with a make date of 10/18/2026. 

CORRECTED- These items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS food items that are prepared or opened in-house are discarded or used within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following TCS foods were observed to not be date-marked:

1. The milk in the outside bar that was opened Sunday. 
2. The milk in the clear double-door cooler that was opened yesterday. 
3. The tamales in the clear double-cooler that were pulled from the freezer two days ago. 
4. The lettuce in the clear double-door cooler that was prepared yesterday. 
5. The various flavored creamers that were opened on Sunday. 

CORRECTED- The PIC dated the items during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods that are opened or prepared in-house and are held for more than 24 hours are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded or used by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility uses ice baths during lunch for TCS food items on the cook-line. The ice bath for sauces only reached a quarter of the way up the bottles of sauces. The ice bath for burger toppings (lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles) and other food items, such as coleslaw, was only ice and only touched the bottom of the container. Coleslaw probed to be at 51.9F and ranch probed to be at 52F. The burger toppings probed to be at 49F. These ice baths had been made at 11am. The PIC stated that they checked the temperatures of the food items at 12pm and that they were under 41F. The PIC stated that the sauces and coleslaw are discarded after four hours and that the other items are placed back in the cooler. Ensure that ice baths are properly submerging the bottom of the containers and are a mixture of both ice and water to allow for proper cold holding. These TCS food items need to be maintained at 41F or below unless they will be under Time as Control and discarded after four hours. CORRECTED- A proper ice bath was discussed with the PIC and the TCS items on the line were placed under Time as Control. These items were discarded at 4pm. Ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held at 41F or below.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to use the handwashing sink on the cook line to fill up a bucket. CORRECTED- Educated employee on not using the handwashing sink for anything other than the intended purpose of handwashing. Ensure that employees are educated on handwashing sinks only being used for handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink at the bar was observed to not have any soap at it, the handwashing sink at the server area to the left of the bar was observed to not have paper towels at it, and there was a scratch pad in the handwashing sink at the bar. Ensure that handwashing sinks are always stocked with individual, disposable towels, soap, and are accessible at all times. CORRECTED- Discussed this with the operator and soap and paper towels were provided for the sinks and the scratch pad was removed.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There was beef observed to be stored above 2 lobster tails in the small black cooler along the server line. CORRECTED- The operator switched the storage order of these. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by being in the proper storage order. Proper storage order is as follows: 
1. RTE foods (such as vegetables). 
2. Unwashed vegetables. 
3. Seafood. 
4. Whole cuts of beef and pork.
5. Ground beef and pork. 
6. Whole and ground poultry.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The ice machine was observed to have slight soil residue accumulation in the top of the inside of the machine. CORRECTED- The operator cleaned it during the inspection and they will be reaching out to Pepsi for a deep cleaning of the inside as they clean it more thoroughly. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There are plates and bowls at the buffet table and at the server area to the left of the bar that are not inverted to protect them from contamination. There are also forks in the server area that are stored with the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service utensils, articles, and sanitized utensils are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair: 

1. The ice scoop holder to the left of the server soda machine is in disrepair and has been taped. Tape is not allowed to be used to fix broken equipment due to it not being smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is repaired to allow it to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The sink to the right of the dish machine is in need of being re-caulked. Ensure that this is re-caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The triple sink across from the two-way cooler is in need of being caulked to the wall. Ensure that this is caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
4. REPEAT- There is a piece of trim coming off in the doorway leading to the chemical area. Ensure that this piece of trim is replaced. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities need cleaned: 

1. REPEAT- The floor in the room with the soda syrups is observed to have soda syrup spills on it and food debris. Ensure that this is cleaned to prevent pest harborage. 
2. The floor under the bar underneath the equipment and tables. 
3. The gaskets of the cooler to the right of the handwashing sink along the cook line are in need of being cleaned. 
4. The bottom of the 2-way cooler next to the pizza area. 
5. The bottom of the standing white freezer across from the triple sink. 
6. The cords and radio to the left of the chili station. It is recommended to have a wall or barrier between the two. 

Ensure that these areas are all cleaned and are maintained cleaned. Physical facilities should be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan has dust accumulation on it. 
2. The floor around the soda syrups has debris and some spills on it. 
3. The shelf with dishes on it to the left of the cook line has soil residue on it. 
4. There is dust accumulation above the dish machine in the kitchen. 
5. The wall around the dish machine has soil residue on it. 
6. There is a fan in the dish area that has dust accumulation on it that could potentially contaminate clean dishes in this area. 
7. The bottom of the white standing freezer to the left of the two-way silver standing freezer has food debris in the bottom of it. 

Ensure that these nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned. 

 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a piece of trim coming off in the doorway leading to the chemical area. 
2. The dish shelves in the prep area are beginning to rust and either need sealed or replaced to prevent contamination to clean dishes.

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket by the cook line tested to be at a concentration of 100ppm. The recommended concentration of Quaternary ammonium sanitizer is between 200 and 400ppm. CORRECTED- The buckets were made with water that was too hot. The operator demonstrated this and the buckets were remade. Dispenser was tested to be at 200ppm. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and changed if not at the recommended concentration. 

 Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (Pf)

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: There is bare wood behind the chili hot holding station. Ensure that this bare wood is sealed to allow it be a smooth and non absorbent material. All bare wood that is exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling needs to be sealed. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following areas were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler floors behind shelving. 
2. The walls above the mop sink. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: No certified food manager is present. See that certificates are provided for those managers that have one available. CK attempted to look through facility history and was unable to find prior records for present managers. Contact the issuing agency to have your certificate re-issued. 
(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Facility was unable to product the Norovirus clean-up policy. Provided during the inspection. See that staff keeps available the Norovirus clean-up policy, sick policy, and reporting agreements. 
A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.11: Observed staff outside of cook line to not be using barriers when washing hands. Discussed with PIC. Ensure employees are properly handwashing to prevent recontaminating hands. Discussed with managers for facility and front of house as well. 
2-301.11:  FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Observed multiple hand washing stations to not have paper towels or soap available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure hand washing stations are equipped with soap and paper towel to encourage hand washing and to prevent the spread of food borne illness. 
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed staff dumping liquid down the cook line hand sink. Discussed with staff. Ensure hand washing stations are limited to only handwashing and that they remain unobstructed to encourage handwashing. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-101.11: Observed a can of ripe olives to be heavily dented. Observed with PIC and pulled. Ensure after delivery that cans are in unadulterated condition.  
3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Observed a dirty fan to be blowing on clean dishes near the back dish machine. Discussed with staff and PIC, fan was turned to no longer blow on dishes. Ensure clean dishes are stored in an area that prevents any extra contamination and that the fan is no longer turned toward dishes. 
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed the dish machine in the back to have an accumulation of food debris around the doors. Discussed with PIC. Ensure dish machine is cleaned at a frequency to prevent any buildup of food debris to ensure dishes are properly cleaned. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.12:  The frozen salmon is labeled to remove from packaging prior to thawing. Discussed with cook and packaging was cut during the inspection. Corrected-on-site. See that frozen salmon vacuum packages are broken prior to the start of thawing. 
Frozen TCS FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 41F or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to need maintenance attention:

1) Damaged wood to the right of the bar dish machine (water damage causing wood to warp). Discussed with PIC. 
2) Base of the sliding door cooler in the kitchen is chipping (paint the interior base of the slider cooler);
3) Dish machine room edge of shelves on either end of the dish machine (bare pressed wood).

Ensure surfaces are smooth, non absorbent, and easily cleanable. 
4-101.10:  NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.
